title: How a verifier evaluates an open mandate
caption: The order of checks from the Verification and Processing Rules: the chain first, then unchanged values, then every constraint. An unknown constraint type always fails. Which error a given failure maps to is partly an interpretation: the specification defines the four codes but does not map each individual check to one of them.
alt: Flowchart. Receive open and closed mandates. If the chain does not verify under Delegate SD-JWT (closed mandate signed by the key in cnf, sd_hash matches), return invalid_credential, terminal. If the closed mandate changes a value the open mandate fixed, return invalid_mandate, terminal. Otherwise take each constraint in turn: an unknown type returns unresolved_constraint; a known constraint that is not satisfied or cannot be checked, for example an amount outside amount_range, a payee outside allowed_payees or unmatched line items, also returns unresolved_constraint. When all constraints pass, return a receipt with status Success. unresolved_constraint may signal a fallback to a user-approved closed mandate or a non-agentic flow.
